newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow air cargo stable, but customs rule may disrupt.
newsitem.headline: Moscow air cargo stable, but customs rule may disrupt.

text.p: Air cargo rates from Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport were unchanged over the past four weeks, but a new customs registration threatens to disrupt the market, a Reuters survey showed.

Nikolai Belyayev, senior cargo manager of EMS Garant Post, Air France's cargo agent, said a new customs regulation required exporters based outside Moscow to register cargo at the regional customs office, instead of at Sheremetyevo.

"It may shock the air cargo market," Belyayev said, adding the rule resembled a ban, since lifted, on transit cargo through Moscow airports. But he said the market had not yet reacted to the new registration rule and was stable.
Other forwarders said the new rule said the new customs registration rule could create hassle and red tape.

Boris Panchenko, senior cargo manager at forwarding firm Eruslan, Aeroflot's cargo agent, said there were already fewer shipments in June compared to May, but he attributed the decline to seasonal factors.
"It's the begining of the summer holiday period," he said, referring to the months when Russian workers take vacations.
East-Line cargo airline's official said the market had been slow over the past three weeks, adding the trend would continue until August.
But Igor Mordvinov, senior sales manager of Burlington Air Express Moscow, saw more active business.
"The market was very active in the last four weeks, because most clients were in a hurry to close contracts for the first half of the year," he said. He gave no forecasts for July and August.
"Last year, we expected a weak market in these months, but it was extremely active," he added. "The market is difficult to predict in this country".
Nadezhda Sokolova, senior cargo manager for the Aeroservice forwarder company, saw active shipments to Japanese destinations, Beijing and Hong Kong, but she said the market could slip in July.
Marina Konovalova, commercial director for Icaros International Cargo Service, said her clients preferred to carry cargo through Aeroflot due to its lower rates.
She said the Icaros company planned delivery of oil equipment from Los Angeles to Perm, in the Urals, in August, on an Antonov An-124 heavy freighter.

Mordvinov said U.S. destinations were active for his company this month. But he also said some clients preferred to carry heavy cargo from Moscow to South American destinations by sea ships due to what he said were higher air cargo rates.
"We are seeing a lack of direct cargo flights from Moscow to many long-range destinations, including to South America," he said. - Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
